description.narrative: Cyclone Freddy brought devastating floods, destruction <(>&<)> death to Mozambique. Freddy 1st made landfall on 24 Feb and then again on 11 March through Zambezia to other Provinces with max. winds of 148 km/h <(>&<)> gusts up to 213 km/h. According to 22 March data(INGD), Freddy affected 891,582 people (166 dead <(>&<)> 656 injured): Zambezia (628K), Sofala (140K), Tete (101K), Manica (6K) <(>&<)> Niassa (16K). 128K homes were destroyed, 66K homes partially destroyed <(>&<)> 54K homes flooded. 391K hectares of land were damaged with137K hectares of crops lost. Health facilities <(>&<)> 1630 classrooms were also damaged, affecting 162K students <(>&<)> 3K teachers. Oxfam <(>&<)> partner KULIMA will support flood-affected ppl in Namacura <(>&<)> Maganja da Costa districts in Zambezia with food assistance, Agro support, hygiene <(>&<)> women dignity kit distribution, hygiene promotion, <(>&<)> water pt rehabilitation. Protection is mainstreamed <(>&<)> project is closely coordinated with DRA partners for complementarity."

participating-org.narrative: Oxfam Novib is one of the 17 national affiliates of the Oxfam International Confederation. It started life in 1956 as the Netherlands Organisation for International Assistance (Novib), and joined forces with Oxfam in 1994. Working together in confederation, the Oxfam affiliates can speak with one clear and compelling voice on issues of global concern: climate change, health and education forall, agriculture, trade, and conflicts and emergencies. Oxfam established this country office to support local organizations and projects. Through this local office Oxfam Novib directly contributes towards this project’s implementation.
